title: Dawat Survival
tagline: Eat, praise, refuse seconds, accept chai. Repeat until Eid.
canDo: You can get through a desi dinner as a guest without offending anyone

grammar.title: mujhe … chahiye / pasand hai
grammar.body: Wanting and liking are said backwards: 'mujhe chai chahiye' (to me, tea is needed) and 'mujhe biryani pasand hai' (to me, biryani is liked). 'Mujhe' = to me.

grammar.title: Nouns have gender
grammar.body: Masculine nouns often end in -a (khana, kamra), feminine in -i (roti, chai). Adjectives that end in -a change to match: achha khana, achhi chai, achhe log (plural).

phrases.en: In the name of God (said before eating)

phrases.note: The generic word for any curry with gravy.

phrases.roman: aap ke haath mein bohat zaiqa hai
phrases.urdu: آپ کے ہاتھ میں بہت ذائقہ ہے
phrases.literal: there's great flavour in your hands
phrases.note: The ultimate compliment to the cook. Say this to Nani and you're in the will.
Say it with a hand over your plate. Words alone do not stop a desi host.
Say this immediately. Desi chai default sweetness is 'dentist's retirement fund'.
Every host's battle cry. Means 'stop talking and eat'.

phrases.en: You shouldn't have gone to the trouble!
phrases.note: The guest's ritual line when a lavish spread appears. The host will say 'koi takleef nahin'.

lessons.title: Khana lag gaya!
lessons.blurb: What's on the table, and how to start eating.
lessons.canDo: You can name the food on a desi table

teach.tip: The call to the table. Drop everything. Nobody waits.
Said quietly before the first bite.
Any curry. 'Aaj kya salan hai?' = What curry is it today?

exercises.prompt: You're about to take the first bite. What do you say?
Khala says “Khana lag gaya hai!” What should you do?

options.feedback: Correct. Food waits for no one.
The food is getting cold. Khala's patience is getting colder.
You'll find out. At the table. Go.

lessons.title: Bas, bas!
lessons.blurb: The ancient art of refusing seconds (and thirds).
lessons.canDo: You can stop a host refilling your plate (eventually)

teach.tip: The tactical compromise. Accept a little, stop a lot.

teach.title: The three-no rule
teach.info: A desi host hears your first 'no' as politeness, your second as shyness, and maybe your third as a real no. Hand over the plate helps. Leaving a little food on it helps more.

exercises.prompt: Nani is spooning more rice onto your plate. Stop her!
You said “Ji nahin, shukriya” once. Khala is still holding the serving spoon. Next move?

options.feedback: Textbook. Khala respects a hand over the plate.
Silence is a yes. Here comes more biryani.

lessons.title: Mazedaar!
lessons.blurb: Praise the food. Lavishly. It's the price of admission.
lessons.canDo: You can praise the food and the cook properly

teach.tip: The power move. Elders will repeat it to everyone.
Ask this, then praise whoever made it.

exercises.prompt: Khala asks how the food is.

exercises.situation: Nani made everything from scratch. You want to praise her.

options.feedback: Nani pretends not to be pleased. She is extremely pleased.
Sweet and casual. She'd have liked a bit more ceremony.
You told Nani her food is too spicy. To her face. In her house.

exercises.prompt: You arrive and there are nine dishes on the table. Say the polite thing.

lessons.title: Chai, cheeni kam
lessons.blurb: Accept tea like a pro. Save your teeth.
lessons.canDo: You can ask for tea, water, and less sugar

teach.tip: Never a real question. The chai is already brewing.

teach.title: mujhe … chahiye
teach.info: ‘I want X’ is ‘mujhe X chahiye’: literally ‘to me, X is needed’. The thing you want comes in the middle.

exercises.prompt: What's the most polite way to ask Nani for water?

options.feedback: Fine, but a little blunt for Nani.

lessons.title: Pasand hai
lessons.blurb: What you like, what you don't, and why chai is a 'she'.
lessons.canDo: You can say what you like and don't like to eat

teach.title: mujhe … pasand hai
teach.info: ‘I like X’ is ‘mujhe X pasand hai’: literally ‘to me, X is liked’. Same pattern as chahiye.

teach.title: Food has gender
teach.info: Every noun is masculine or feminine, and adjectives follow. Khana (food) is masculine: khana achha hai. Chai is feminine: chai achhi hai. Words ending in -a are usually masculine; -i usually feminine.

teach.tip: Heads up: 'thori si mirch' in a desi kitchen is not a little.

exercises.prompt: Tell Khala you like biryani (she'll make it every visit now).

lessons.title: Garam garam
lessons.blurb: Hosts' battle cries and how to answer them.
lessons.canDo: You can keep up with a host's running commentary

teach.tip: 'Fresh roti, garam garam!' Accept it. Resistance is futile.

exercises.prompt: Khala says “Khana thanda ho raha hai!” What does she mean?

options.text: Please put it in the microwave

exercises.prompt: The power move: “You cook so well” (in Urdu, respectfully)

boss.title: Nani's Dastarkhwan
boss.blurb: Nani has cooked for eleven. There are four of you. Survive dinner.
boss.scene: Sunday at Nani's. The table bends under biryani, two salans, daal, fresh roti and a mountain of kebabs. Nani sits at the head, watching your plate like a hawk.
boss.canDo: You can survive a full desi meal: eat, praise, refuse seconds, and accept chai

options.reaction: Nani waves it away, delighted that you know the script.

c.text: Ten minutes later. Your plate has been refilled twice without you noticing. Nani reaches for the biryani again.

options.reaction: A tactical 'thora sa'. She gives you a large thora sa.

diet3.text: The word 'diet' has been noted. Two extra kebabs land on your plate as punishment.

options.reaction: Nani suppresses a smile. You are now officially her favourite.
Nani accepts your correction. The silence before it will haunt you.
'Cheeni kam' noted. She adds two spoons anyway, but smaller ones.
You get the standard four sugars. Godspeed.

end.title: Dinner survived
end.text: You ate, praised, refused (sort of), and accepted chai. Nani will tell the whole family you 'eat like a proper bacha now'. That's a compliment.
